findings.message: Reusable workflow node 'Workflow1:SetRate' (Elsa.SetVariable) becomes an Elsa 4 engine intrinsic, which a graph activity cannot hold yet.
findings.guidance: Elsa 4 graph activities have no Set Variable yet (tracked in elsa-foundation#3023). A reusable workflow's variables are its own, so only its body can read them. If nothing in the body reads this variable, remove the Set Variable: nothing else changes. If a value only needs to pass from one activity to the next, capture that activity's output into the variable instead, or set it from a Run JavaScript activity's script (setVariable('name', value)), which a reusable body supports. Otherwise keep the workflow in Elsa 3 until elsa-foundation#3023 is done, or clear 'Usable as activity' on this workflow in Elsa 3 and re-export: it then imports as a regular workflow, and every workflow that uses it as an activity must call it with Dispatch Workflow or Execute Workflow instead. The import does not carry the called workflow's outputs over: a captured Execute Workflow result is refused (ELS3-ACTIVITY-OUTPUT-NOT-REPRESENTABLE). A caller that uses an output reads it after import from the Elsa 4 Dispatch Workflow's Result, which holds the outputs when it waits for completion.

findings.message: Variable 'AuditTrail' used the custom Elsa 3 storage driver 'Acme.Storage.BlobStorageDriver, Acme.Storage', which kept its value outside the workflow instance. The converter does not carry storage drivers over: the variable converts to Elsa 4's default storage (elsa.json), so its value is now stored with the workflow instance.
findings.guidance: Decide whether the value may live in the workflow instance. If it must stay in the driver's storage (such as a blob store), plan an Elsa 4 solution for that need before the workflow runs in production. docs/migration/elsa3-storage-drivers.md walks through the choices.

findings.message: Variable 'SessionToken' used the Elsa 3 Memory storage driver ('Elsa.Workflows.MemoryStorageDriver, Elsa.Workflows.Core'), which never persisted its value. The variable converts to Elsa 4's default storage (elsa.json), so its value is now persisted with the workflow instance.
findings.guidance: Decide why the Memory driver was chosen. If the value must never be persisted (a secret, a token, a large or short-lived value), change the workflow so the variable does not hold it; otherwise the default storage is fine. docs/migration/elsa3-storage-drivers.md walks through the choices.
